pages.title: Scrub and damage: forward scrub (ScrubStack), repair, data uninlining, DamageTable

features.name: Forward scrub start (scrub start command)
features.description: Admin-triggered online scrub from a path with options force/recursive/repair/scrub_mdsdir and optional tag; only on rank 0 and only when active; runs as internal request ENQUEUE_SCRUB with DISCOVER|RDLOCK_PATH traversal; replies {return_code, scrub_tag, mode: asynchronous} with command rc 0.
features.notes: Errors returned in JSON return_code: -EBUSY (inode already scrubbing), -EEXIST (tag active), -EAGAIN (abort in progress), traversal errors (-ENOENT, -EIO, -ESTALE for relative paths). Non-rank-0: -EXDEV; not active: -EINVAL.

features.name: Recursive scrub traversal (ScrubStack deque, breadth-first)
features.description: Dirfrags pushed to the front, child inodes to the back of an intrusive list; kick_off_scrubs processes items until mds_max_scrub_ops_in_progress async validations/parked items; directory inode validated as soon as its dirfrags are queued; every queued object holds PIN_SCRUBQUEUE, dirfrags also an auth pin.
features.notes: Breadth-first order pins whole tree levels in cache; no heartbeat resets in the dentry loop.

features.name: Incremental scrub (skip unchanged dentries unless force)
features.description: Without force, dentries whose version <= dirfrag last_recursive scrub version are skipped (including subdirectories, since remote_d_type is 0 for primaries); stamps kept in CDir::scrub_info_t and persisted lazily into fnode recursive_scrub_version/stamp.

features.name: Backtrace validation
features.description: Reads xattr 'parent' on <ino>.00000000 in the file layout pool (files) or metadata pool (dirs), decodes and compares with the in-memory ancestry via inode_backtrace_t::compare; tolerates dirty-parent, nlink==0, replica ancestors, mdsdir; failure records BACKTRACE damage.
features.notes: Backtraces are what make lookup-by-ino (NFS handles) and hard-link resolution work.

features.name: Backtrace repair
features.description: With repair, a failed backtrace is rewritten by mark_dirty_parent on the current log segment (written when that segment expires; no journal event) and the BACKTRACE damage entry is removed. The trim_all() at tag completion is best effort: it does not flush the journal first, stops with an ignored -EAGAIN at a segment with pending events, and never expires the current segment.

features.name: InoTable 'inode wrongly marked free' check and repair
features.description: Checks the local rank's InoTable free/projected_free sets for the scrubbed ino; with repair removes it (only if no projections in flight) and saves the table.

features.name: Base inode on-disk validation (root, ~mdsN)
features.description: Fetches the persisted base inode into a shadow CInode and compares with inode_t::compare; failure only logged (no damage entry, no repair).
features.notes: The fetch rval is recorded but not checked: a missing .inode object (and no legacy xattr) leaves the shadow at its create_unlinked_system_inode defaults and normally passes (by code reading).

features.name: Directory dirstat/rstat validation and repair
features.description: Sums dirfrags' accounted_fragstat/accounted_rstat (+1 rsubdirs, +snaps) and compares with inode dirstat/rstat; forces scatter-gather first (RDLOCK_FRAGSSTATS) if any dirfrag is a subtree root; mismatch forgiven when the inode, a local auth dirfrag, or (per the last OP_QUEUEDIR_ACK) a remote dirfrag is dirty; repair runs REPAIR_INODESTATS, which marks the scatterlocks dirty and rdlocks them to force a scatter-gather. finish_scatter_gather_update always adopts the dirfrag sums when all leaves are cached; STATE_REPAIRSTATS only suppresses the 'unmatched fragstat'/'inconsistent rstat' clog errors and the mds_verify_scatter assert.
features.notes: Directory nlink/st_size-like values visible to clients derive from these stats (rstat for ceph.dir.r* vxattrs and quotas).

features.name: Dirfrag fragstat/rstat validation and repair
features.description: check_rstats(true) compares fnode fragstat/rstat with sums over head children; repair journals EUpdate('repair_dirfrag') with recomputed stats and removes all DENTRY damage entries of that dirfrag.

features.name: Dentry first/last corruption detection
features.description: CDentry::scrub flags first > global snap seq + 1 or first > last; check_corruption flags first > last or first > snapclient last_seq + 1 on every add_{null,primary,remote}_dentry (load=true) and before commit (load=false; mds_go_bad_corrupt_dentry, mds_abort_on_newly_corrupt_dentry); registers DENTRY damage via go_bad_dentry.
features.notes: first-damage.py finds the first > next-snap subset offline (it does not check first > last).

features.name: Hard-link resolvability check
features.description: For remote dentries whose target is not cached and not known-damaged, open_remote_dentry (backtrace-based open_ino); failure sets STATE_BADREMOTEINO and BACKTRACE damage; not repairable.
features.notes: POSIX hard links must resolve.

features.name: Scrub tags
features.description: User tag (or generated UUID marked internal); user tags are written as xattr scrub_tag (ceph-encoded std::string) on each inode's first object; tag identifies the scrub in status and completion protocol; duplicate active tag -> -EEXIST.
features.notes: Consumed by cephfs-data-scan --filter-tag and cls cephfs PGLS filter on _scrub_tag.

features.name: tag path command
features.description: Forced recursive scrub (no repair) with the given tag; synchronous enqueue on the admin-socket thread; rank 0 only.

features.name: ~mdsdir / ~mdsN scrubbing and scrub_mdsdir
features.description: Path ~mdsdir means the executing rank's mdsdir, ~mdsN rank N's; scrub_mdsdir with path / additionally queues rank 0's own mdsdir on top. Loading stray dirs lets the generic stray evaluation act on them.
features.notes: Documented as a way to evaluate strays (doc/cephfs/scrub.rst).

features.name: Data uninlining during scrub
features.description: Every scrubbed non-directory inode gets internal request UNINLINE_DATA: xlock authlock/filelock/versionlock, then if inline data exists write it to <ino>.00000000 (create + cmpxattr inline_version GT + write + setxattr inline_version=u64max) and journal EUpdate('uninline') clearing inline_data; failures aggregated per tag and turned into UNINLINE damage on rank 0.
features.notes: Inline data is deprecated; only created when fs flag inline_data is set and client has CEPH_FEATURE_MDS_INLINE_DATA (src/mds/Server.cc:3758). cmpxattr operand bug: encodes InodeStoreBase instead of u64. In the xlock states clients keep only Fc/Fb (filelock) and no As/Ax (authlock).

features.name: Multi-rank work forwarding
features.description: Non-auth dirfrags forwarded with MMDSScrub OP_QUEUEDIR (ack OP_QUEUEDIR_ACK with queued frags and dirty flag); non-auth inodes with OP_QUEUEINO (ack OP_QUEUEINO_ACK); waits on ambiguous auth or degraded cluster.
features.notes: MDS-to-MDS only; not a contract for the Rust MDS (no mixing with C++ daemons). The dirty-remote-dirfrag flag is taken only from the last OP_QUEUEDIR_ACK to arrive.

features.name: Multi-rank completion protocol (scrub epochs)
features.description: Rank 0 tick sends MMDSScrubStats(epoch) to all up ranks; peers reply with locally active tags plus uninline failures/counters; a tag finishes when inactive locally and unreported across two consecutive fully acked epochs; epoch_last_forwarded bridges forwarding windows.
features.notes: Liveness depends on every up rank answering; slots exist for every rank up to the highest up rank, so a failed rank numbered below it (no replacement daemon) stalls tag completion (by code reading).

features.name: Scrub pause / resume / abort
features.description: State machine IDLE/RUNNING/PAUSING/PAUSED with clear_stack abort flag; deferred completion until in-flight ops drain; rank 0 broadcasts OP_ABORT/OP_PAUSE/OP_RESUME without acks; resume returns bool (error shows as 1).

features.name: Scrub status, summary, mgr task status, cluster log
features.description: scrub status JSON {status, scrubs{tag:{path,tag,options}}, scrub_stats}; scrub_summary string to clog on changes and to mgr ServiceMap task status key 'scrub status' every mds_task_status_update_interval while not idle.
features.notes: QA polls 'no active scrubs running'. Status also has PAUSING+ABORTING; the options string omits the comma after 'force' (force+scrub_mdsdir prints 'forcescrub_mdsdir').

features.name: Scrub counters and purge_status
features.description: Per-tag uninline counters (started/passed/failed/skipped) aggregated on rank 0, purged by 'scrub purge_status <tag|all>' or after mds_scrub_stats_review_period days.
features.notes: Review period option is not a tracked config key.

features.name: Scrub stamps persistence
features.description: Inode last_scrub_version/stamp and fnode recursive/localized scrub version/stamp kept in scrub_info and copied into the next projected inode/fnode; no dedicated write.

features.name: Scrub throttle
features.description: mds_max_scrub_ops_in_progress (default 5) bounds async validations plus parked objects per rank.
features.notes: Uninline requests and synchronous dirfrag scans are not counted.

features.name: DamageTable registry
features.description: Per-rank in-memory registry of DIRFRAG (ino,frag), DENTRY (ino,frag,dname,snapid), BACKTRACE (ino), UNINLINE_FILE (ino) entries with random 32-bit ids; bounded by mds_damage_table_max_entries; not persisted.

features.name: Damage-driven EIO on request paths
features.description: path_traverse returns -EIO for damaged dirfrags, damaged dentries, and uncached remote dentries pointing to backtrace-damaged inos; fetch waiters get -EIO and retry into these checks.
features.notes: EIO is the POSIX-visible error for unreadable metadata.

features.name: readdir behaviour with damage
features.description: Undecodable dentries are absent; remote dentries with STATE_BADREMOTEINO are skipped; a BADFRAG dirfrag is complete so readdir succeeds with cached entries only (normally empty); no EIO from readdir.
features.notes: By code reading.

features.name: Fatal damage marks rank damaged
features.description: notify_* returns fatal for own mdsdir/stray dentries, own stray or root dirfrags, or table overflow; fetch-path callers then call MDSRank::damaged() (want-state down:damaged, flush clog, beacon send_and_wait, respawn).
features.notes: Scrub backtrace/inode results and uninline failures ignore the fatal result; CDentry::scrub goes through go_bad_dentry and honours it. Damage to the rank's own mdsdir dirfrag is not fatal, and populate_mydir's recreate branch (get_version()==0 && BADFRAG) is unreachable because go_bad gives BADFRAG dirfrags a version-1 fnode.

features.name: MDS_DAMAGE health
features.description: Beacon health metric MDS_HEALTH_DAMAGE (HEALTH_ERR 'Metadata damage detected') whenever the table is non-empty; mon check MDS_DAMAGE merged with the damaged-rank check of the same code.

features.name: damage ls / damage rm
features.description: damage ls dumps the per-rank table as a JSON array {damage_type, id, ino, frag, dname, snap_id, rank, errno, scrub_tag, path}; damage rm <id> erases by id (silent if missing).
features.notes: Erasing a dentry entry drops all dentry entries of that dirfrag from the lookup index.

features.name: Dirfrag load damage detection
features.description: Missing dirfrag object or undecodable fnode -> go_bad (DIR_FRAG, synthetic fnode, BADFRAG, complete, waiters -EIO); undecodable dentry -> go_bad_dentry (DENTRY); other read errors assert.
features.notes: With the non-default mds_dir_prefetch=false, a keyed dentry fetch that hits a missing object calls go_bad(false), which wakes only WAIT_COMPLETE waiters, so requests parked in waiting_on_dentry are not resumed (by code reading).

features.name: Directory backtrace verification on fetch
features.description: When mds_verify_backtrace > 0, fetching frag * of a directory also reads its parent xattr; an unreadable xattr or a mismatched first ancestor logs a clog error and schedules a rewrite (mark_dirty_parent + mdlog flush); >1 asserts. Skipped for base, dirty-parent and non-auth inodes. The decode has no try/catch.

features.name: Read-only mode on RADOS write errors
features.description: mds_action_on_write_error=1 (default) -> MDCache::force_readonly: EROFS for write requests, CEPH_SESSION_FORCE_RO to clients, write caps revoked, journal trimming stops, MDS_READ_ONLY health; never cleared until restart.
features.notes: Not triggered by damage-table entries.

features.name: flush_path command
features.description: Internal request FLUSH: rdlock path, CInode::flush stores dirty backtrace and commits the parent dirfrag or base inode; -EROFS if read-only, -EXDEV if not auth.

features.name: Scrub-triggered fragmentation
features.description: After each dirfrag scan, MDBalancer::maybe_fragment(dir, false) may queue split/merge; scrubbing dirfrags refuse fragmentation (can_fragment).

features.name: Journal flush after repairs
features.description: When a tag that performed repairs is retired on a rank, MDLog::trim_all() (trim_to(0)) starts expiry of all but the newest segment so repaired metadata reaches RADOS; best effort (no prior flush, -EAGAIN ignored, current segment kept).

features.name: Lookup-by-ino failure semantics
features.description: LOOKUPINO failing in open_ino returns -ESTALE (ENOENT/ENODATA mapped) and does not create damage entries.
features.notes: NFS handle staleness.

features.name: Duplicate primary inode detection on dirfrag load
features.description: A primary dentry whose ino is already cached under another dentry logs clog error 'loaded dup inode ... already exists at ...' and is not linked (absent from listings); no damage-table entry unless mds_hack_allow_loading_invalid_metadata links it anyway.
features.notes: Silent namespace loss from the client's view; only the cluster log shows it.

features.name: Repair of dirfrag stats without damage check
features.description: repair_dirfrag_stats_work recomputes and journals fnode fragstat/rstat from the cached dentries of any complete dirfrag, including a BADFRAG one that scrub_dirfrag scanned after its own full fetch failed (C_RetryScrub ignores the error).
features.notes: By code reading.

serialization_points.name: Rank-global ScrubStack under mds_lock
serialization_points.shared_state: scrub_stack, scrub_waiting, scrubbing_map, remote_scrubs, scrubs_in_progress, counters
serialization_points.why_serialized: Single per-rank object; every enqueue, kick, completion, message and control op asserts mds_lock
serialization_points.notes: Different tags/subtrees share only these containers.

serialization_points.name: Scrub throttle
serialization_points.why_serialized: Bounds concurrent async validations and parked items per rank across all tags

serialization_points.name: One scrub per inode / per dirfrag
serialization_points.why_serialized: Only one header slot per object; second enqueue gets -EBUSY (ignored for children)
serialization_points.notes: Overlapping tags silently skip already-scrubbing inodes.

serialization_points.name: Dirfrag auth pin while queued
serialization_points.why_serialized: Keeps dirfrag in cache and unfrozen during scan; blocks freeze for export/fragmentation
serialization_points.notes: can_fragment also refuses dirfrags with scrub in progress (src/mds/MDCache.cc:11903).

serialization_points.name: Uninline xlocks on every scrubbed file
serialization_points.shared_state: authlock, filelock, versionlock of the file
serialization_points.notes: Revokes client caps on every scrubbed file; inherent only for inodes that actually have inline data.

serialization_points.name: Stat stabilisation rdlocks (RDLOCK_FRAGSSTATS)
serialization_points.why_serialized: Forces scatter-gather so accounted dirfrag stats are current before comparing
serialization_points.notes: Directory-wide, across ranks holding its dirfrags; only for dirs with subtree-root dirfrags.

serialization_points.name: Inode stats repair (REPAIR_INODESTATS)
serialization_points.why_serialized: wrlock + mark updated + rdlock to force scatter-gather that overwrites inode stats

serialization_points.name: Dirfrag stats repair (REPAIR_FRAGSTATS)
serialization_points.shared_state: dir inode dirfragtreelock (rd), nestlock/filelock (wr), dirfrag fnode
serialization_points.why_serialized: Project and journal corrected fnode stats

serialization_points.name: InoTable repair
serialization_points.why_serialized: Refuses while any projection is in flight
serialization_points.notes: Only the one ino conflicts logically.

serialization_points.name: trim_all after repairing tag
serialization_points.why_serialized: Expire all segments to flush repaired metadata

serialization_points.name: Rank 0 scrub coordinator
serialization_points.why_serialized: All commands accepted only on rank 0; completion via rank-0-driven epochs; rank 0 failure aborts all
serialization_points.notes: Completion of a tag depends only on ranks holding its work.

serialization_points.name: DamageTable per rank
serialization_points.shared_state: dirfrags, dentries, remotes, uninline_failures, by_id maps
serialization_points.why_serialized: Single structure protected by mds_lock; consulted on every path_traverse step
serialization_points.notes: Entries are naturally keyed per dirfrag/ino.

serialization_points.name: Synchronous dirfrag scans under mds_lock
serialization_points.why_serialized: Dentry loop and multi-dirfrag kick pass run without yielding or heartbeat resets

serialization_points.name: MDSRank::damaged() swan song
serialization_points.why_serialized: Blocks under mds_lock up to mds_mon_shutdown_timeout, then respawns
serialization_points.notes: Rank-level state is the only damage granularity the mon understands.

serialization_points.name: Uninline request blocked on client cap revocation
serialization_points.shared_state: file inode authlock/filelock xlock state, tag num_pending
serialization_points.why_serialized: The tag's num_pending only drops after the uninline request (unthrottled, not counted in scrubs_in_progress) gets its xlocks, which waits for every client holding conflicting caps
serialization_points.notes: A slow client on one file delays completion of the whole tag.

external_contract.detail: ceph tell mds.<fs>:0 scrub start <path> [force|recursive|repair|scrub_mdsdir] [tag]; rank 0 only (-EXDEV), active only (-EINVAL); reply JSON {return_code, scrub_tag, mode:'asynchronous'}; after those checks the command rc is always 0 and enqueue errors appear only in return_code.

{status: 'no active scrubs running' | 'IDLE (waiting for more scrubs)' | 'scrub active (N inodes in the stack)' | 'ABORTING (...)' | 'PAUSING (...)' | 'PAUSED (...)' | 'PAUSING+ABORTING (...)' | 'PAUSED+ABORTING (...)', scrubs: {tag: {path, tag, options}}, scrub_stats (rank 0): {tag: {start_time, path, uninline_started, uninline_passed, uninline_failed, uninline_skipped}}}.
Rank 0 only; abort/pause reply {message, return_code} after local drain; pause during abort -EINVAL; resume reply {return_code} (error appears as 1); purge_status <tag|all>.

damage ls: JSON array of {damage_type: dir_frag|dentry|backtrace|uninline, id, ino, frag ('*' or binary prefix), dname, snap_id ('head' or hex), rank, errno (string), scrub_tag, path}; damage rm <damage_id> (CephInt).
tag path <path> <tag>: forced recursive scrub writing scrub_tag xattrs (rank 0). flush_path <path>: write backtrace and parent dirfrag of an auth inode; {message, return_code}.
MCommand from a session without allow_all() gets -EACCES 'permission denied'.
Beacon health metric MDS_HEALTH_DAMAGE (HEALTH_ERR, 'Metadata damage detected') while the damage table is non-empty; mon check code MDS_DAMAGE, summary '%num% MDSs report damaged metadata'.
Fatal damage sets beacon want-state STATE_DAMAGED and waits up to mds_mon_shutdown_timeout for the ack before respawning; mon puts the rank in the damaged set until 'ceph mds repaired'.
Beacon metric MDS_HEALTH_READ_ONLY (HEALTH_WARN 'MDS in read-only mode') after a write error with mds_action_on_write_error=1.

clog info 'scrub queued for path: P', 'scrub summary: S', 'Scrub repaired inode I (P)'; warn 'Scrub error on inode|dir|dentry ...', 'bad backtrace on inode ..., rewriting it'; error 'dir D object missing on disk; some files may be lost', 'scrub: inode wrongly marked free: I', etc.
Every mds_task_status_update_interval (2 s) while not idle, key 'scrub status' with summary 'active paths [/]' etc.; shown by ceph status under task status.

mds.scrub_backtrace_fetch, scrub_set_tag, scrub_backtrace_repaired, scrub_inotable_repaired, scrub_dir_inodes, scrub_dir_base_inodes, scrub_dirfrag_rstats, scrub_file_inodes (u64 gauges); mds_cache.uninline_started/succeeded/write_failed, ireq_enqueue_scrub/flush/fragstats/inodestats (counters).
getxattr 'parent' (inode_backtrace_t encoding) on <ino hex>.00000000 in the file layout pool (files) or metadata pool (directories).
setxattr 'scrub_tag' = ceph-encoded std::string (u32 length + bytes) on the inode's first object for user tags; creates the object if absent.
create(non-exclusive); cmpxattr('inline_version', GT, U64, operand) + write(0, data, truncate_size, truncate_seq) + setxattr('inline_version', '18446744073709551615') with the realm snap context.
PGLS filter 'inode_tag' of class cephfs selects *.00000000 objects whose _scrub_tag xattr decodes to a string different from the requested tag.
Requests whose path walk hits a damaged dirfrag, damaged dentry, or uncached hard link to a backtrace-damaged ino get -EIO.
Undecodable dentries and STATE_BADREMOTEINO remote dentries are omitted; BADFRAG dirfrags list as empty (no error).
Uninline request xlocks authlock/filelock/versionlock on every scrubbed file, revoking conflicting caps until the request completes.

Cap grants carry inline_version = CEPH_INLINE_NONE (accepted because >= cached); object xattr inline_version=u64::MAX so a later uninline by a client still caching an older inline version gets -ECANCELED, which the kernel treats as success. Clients set the xattr to the decimal of their own version.
On read-only transition the MDS sends MClientSession(FORCE_RO) to open/stale client sessions; kernel sets s_readonly and returns -EROFS when Fw/Fx are needed.
LOOKUPINO resolves inodes through backtraces; missing backtrace -> -ESTALE; scrub validates/repairs backtraces.
Client::uninline_data uses the same create + cmpxattr(inline_version GT u64) + write + setxattr sequence.
Untagged-only scans (scan_inodes, scan_frags, cleanup) skip first objects whose scrub_tag equals the filter tag (decoded as ceph string).
qa/tasks/cephfs/filesystem.py waits for 'no active scrubs running' in scrub status and reads scrubs[tag] and damage ls.

rust_implications.implication: Operators, QA and docs drive scrub via 'ceph tell mds.<fs>:0 scrub start|status|abort|pause|resume|purge_status', 'damage ls|rm', 'tag path', 'flush_path'. Keep names, argument schemas and JSON field names (return_code, scrub_tag, mode, status, scrubs{path,tag,options}, scrub_stats) and accept them on rank 0 (or any rank) even if internals are per-shard.

Make scrub a per-subvolume/shard background job with its own queue, throttle and QoS budget instead of a rank-global stack and a global rank-0 epoch protocol; a tag's completion can be tracked with explicit per-shard work accounting (credits/acks) since forwarding already has acks.

C++ BFS pins entire tree levels (PIN_SCRUBQUEUE) and loads every dirfrag; use a cursor-based iteration over the shard's on-disk directory index with bounded in-flight state and no requirement to keep scanned inodes cached.

rust_implications.topic: Do not lock files without inline data
rust_implications.implication: C++ xlocks authlock/filelock/versionlock on every scrubbed file, revoking client caps; a Rust scrub should be read-only against client-visible state except for objects actually being repaired.

A fresh Rust filesystem has no inline data if it always creates inodes with inline_version=CEPH_INLINE_NONE (as C++ does when the inline_data flag is off); uninline-on-scrub can then be omitted. If the inline_data fs flag must be honoured, follow the kclient/libcephfs protocol (cmpxattr inline_version GT with an 8-byte LE u64 operand, setxattr decimal) and do not copy the C++ operand bug.

Keep a damage registry so repeated access to known-bad metadata fails fast with EIO; shard it per subvolume/dirfrag and consider persisting it (C++ loses it on restart). Keep MDS_HEALTH_DAMAGE semantics in the beacon (HEALTH_ERR while any entry exists) because the mon only understands rank-level metrics.

C++ escalates some damage to the whole rank (down:damaged). The mon only has rank-level damaged state; a Rust MDS that wants per-subvolume isolation must express shard damage through health metrics/EIO for that shard rather than the rank state, and reserve down:damaged for rank-wide structures.

CEPH_SESSION_FORCE_RO is per MDS session and the kernel then refuses Fw/Fx for every inode whose auth cap is from that session; a per-shard read-only mode cannot be expressed to kclients unless shards map to different MDS sessions/ranks. Per-shard write errors could instead fail only that shard's mutations with EROFS/EIO.

Preserve: -EIO for damaged dirfrags/dentries/hard-link targets on path walks; readdir omits undecodable entries (C++ does not fail readdir); -ESTALE for lookup-by-ino when the inode cannot be located (NFS handles via Ganesha).

Because the Rust on-disk format is free, backtraces in data pools are not required by peers except offline tools; but lookup-by-ino (Ganesha handles, kclient LOOKUPINO/LOOKUPHASH after MDS restart) needs some ino->location index; scrub should validate whatever index replaces backtraces.

rstat/dirstat validation needs a consistent snapshot of child stats; with per-shard transactional journaling, compute and compare within a shard transaction rather than forcing cross-rank scatter-gather; repairs should be journaled in the owning shard's journal and not require trim_all of a global journal.

scrub_tag xattrs and damage_flags only matter for cephfs-data-scan / cls cephfs filter compatibility, which cannot work against a new on-disk format anyway; they can be dropped unless the Rust project ships its own recovery tools.

uninline cmpxattr operand encodes InodeStoreBase; notify_uninline_failed records global errno; abort leaks PIN_SCRUBQUEUE; mdsdir-origin uninline skip leaks auth pin/num_pending; scrub resume returns bool; dentry-entry erase drops the whole dirfrag's dentry index; random 32-bit damage ids can collide; mds_scrub_stats_review_period not runtime-tracked.; dirty-remote-dirfrag flag taken only from the last OP_QUEUEDIR_ACK; scrub status options string missing a separator after 'force'; populate_mydir recreate branch unreachable for BADFRAG mdsdir dirfrags; stat repair does not check the damage table; base-inode check ignores the fetch error; keyed fetches of damaged dirfrags never wake dentry waiters (mds_dir_prefetch=false).
C++ completion requires every up rank to ack two consecutive epochs, so one hung rank stalls all tags; per-shard completion tracking avoids coupling unrelated tenants.

C++ scans entire dirfrags and multiple dirfrags per kick under mds_lock without yielding; the Rust scheduler should scan in bounded batches on the worker pool so scrub never starves client requests of the same shard.
The first/last checks (first <= last, first <= next snap seq) are cheap invariants worth enforcing at write time (C++ aborts before committing newly corrupt dentries by default).

open_questions: Must the Rust MDS support the deprecated inline_data fs flag at all (MDSMap inline_data_enabled set via 'ceph fs set ... inline_data')? If not, what should it do when the mon map says it is enabled?
Is compatibility with cephfs-data-scan/first-damage.py/cephfs-journal-tool required in any form, given the on-disk format is free?
Should the damage table be persisted per shard so MDS_DAMAGE survives restarts (C++ forgets it)?
Do tools or orchestration (cephadm/rook) parse 'scrub status' or 'damage ls' output beyond QA tests? (No mgr module consumer found in src/pybind/mgr.)
readdir of a BADFRAG dirfrag returning an empty listing with success is derived from code reading only; confirm whether clients/tests rely on it or whether EIO would be acceptable.
kclient behaviour on -EIO from lookup/readdir beyond pass-through to user space was not examined in detail (unverified).
